admission.mechanism: Proposed independent boundary: one fenced active PgBouncer for the selected database, with a global database backend-session ceiling of 40 and user backend-session ceilings of 34 API, 4 workers and 2 maintenance. All SQL clients must use it; deny direct database paths and bypass roles. Configure these as backend/server connection limits, not client limits; bound queue length and wait time and fail closed on exhaustion. Multiple proxy replicas must not each receive these budgets: fence and disconnect the old proxy before replacement activation. Per-process API pools are 3; even extra Cloud Run processes cannot raise the proxy's 40-session ceiling. Exact pooler version/configuration and enforcement remain unverified.

state.authority: Proposed single-writer transactional relational database primary for credential/session epochs, revocations, inventory, reservations and idempotency records. Every protected operation reads current authorization from this authority; KV is only a nonauthoritative display/config cache. Fail closed when authority is unavailable. Durable Objects are a possible per-object coordination alternative, not a claim of cross-object or SQL atomicity.
state.writeOwnership: Cloud Run API is the sole domain mutation path; workers use the same transactional contracts and scoped roles. In one transaction, lock authorization/version rows in a fixed order, verify current credentials, and conditionally decrement all inventory rows with nonnegative constraints, persisting the idempotency result. Revocation locks the same authorization row and increments its epoch; acknowledge only after earlier conflicting transactions/effects are drained. No positive authorization cache, stale replica, KV fallback or edge-only enforcement; protect direct-origin and worker routes. One fenced primary and monotonically increasing ownership epoch across promotion.

checks.requirement: Enforce 40-session boundary regardless of actual process count
checks.mechanism: Single active fenced proxy, global database ceiling 40 and API/worker/maintenance backend ceilings 34/4/2; network and roles deny all bypasses.
checks.limit: All API revisions, jobs, migrations and maintenance use this boundary. A second independently budgeted proxy is prohibited; fail closed during uncertain ownership.
checks.failure: Dual active proxies, ignored server limits, reconnect storms, extra user/database pool combinations, stale sockets or a direct route exceed budget.
checks.verification: Before acceptance, burst beyond nine API processes during rollout, termination and proxy failover; exhaust every role and count actual database sessions. Demonstrate bounded rejection/wait, no leaks, no direct-path bypass, old-session disconnection and total <=40.

checks.mechanism: Authoritative transactional authorization for every protected operation; KV carries no grant authority.
checks.limit: KV changes can be stale for 60 seconds or more, including cached misses; local read-after-write is not guaranteed.
checks.failure: Original KV-only authority can accept revoked credentials at another edge location.
checks.verification: Read Cloudflare KV consistency documentation. This is a documented design failure, not an executed revocation test.

checks.mechanism: Serialize authorization and protected commit with revocation on the same principal/session epoch row. Deny old tokens after acknowledged revocation. Drain or cancel long-lived and asynchronous protected effects before acknowledging revocation; fail closed on missing current authority.
checks.limit: No operation ordered after revocation may be authorized with its old epoch. Revocation acknowledgement waits for earlier effects. Exact in-flight stream/external-effect contract needs confirmation and implementation.
checks.failure: Check-then-use race, stale replica/cache, direct origin access, background job, old signing key or failover restoring an old credential epoch re-enables access.
checks.verification: From multiple edge locations, race revoke against reads, writes, streams and worker effects; use old and latest credentials through edge and direct-origin routes. Partition authority, restart services, rotate signing/DB secrets, and restore stale state; prove denied access and current-key availability without logging secrets.

checks.mechanism: One database transaction owns all affected stock/reservation rows, authorization locks, nonnegative checks and durable idempotency result; use consistent lock order and retry transaction conflicts.
checks.limit: Multi-item operations remain inside one selected database transaction. External effects require a transactional outbox with replay-safe consumers; no cross-object atomicity inferred from Durable Objects.
checks.failure: KV read-modify-write loses updates; partial multi-item commits, duplicate retries or crash after commit can oversell or apply twice.
checks.verification: Race buyers for final units and multi-item orders; inject crash/timeout before and after commit, retry identical keys, and inspect durable stock and operation records. Require exactly one result, no negative stock and all-or-none changes.

checks.requirement: Recovery RTO <=900s and RPO <=60s without unsafe authority
checks.mechanism: Propose warm recovery compute/config/image and a chosen database standby plus isolated backups/PITR. Track durable replay watermarks and independently available latest secrets/keys and revocation watermark. Fence old writers and proxy, establish new ownership epoch, confirm replica eligibility and credentials, then promote state, validate invariants and restore routing. Fail back deliberately with the same fencing.
checks.limit: Promotion requires verified durable acknowledged-write gap <=60s, not average lag. Unknown/excess lag or inability to fence blocks promotion. Stale recovered authorization must never grant access: reconcile to the latest durable revocation ledger/watermark, or invalidate all existing sessions and require fresh authenticated credentials while keeping access closed. The revocation checkpoint must survive the failed domain before acknowledgement; asynchronous RPO alone cannot preserve revocation.
checks.failure: Old-primary split brain, unavailable new secrets, replaying old revocations, missing acknowledged orders, unknown lag, inaccessible backups or DNS/connection cache delay invalidates safe recovery.
checks.verification: In an authorized isolated drill, lose primary region plus dependencies, prove old-writer fencing, recover with latest credentials, inspect commit/replay and revocation watermarks, reconcile acknowledged inventory effects and test routing with reused connections. Measure detection-to-useful-secure-service RTO and lost acknowledged-write interval RPO, including restoration, validation and routing. Repeat failback; retain failures. No drill or measurement exists.

checks.mechanism: Cloudflare edge forwards authenticated requests to Cloud Run; origin validates trusted ingress identity and performs authoritative domain authorization. Regional DB/proxy availability and useful capacity must cover admitted demand after the declared failure.
checks.limit: Cloudflare global routing does not make a regional origin/database globally recoverable. Region, zones, engine, plans, quotas, residency, network and latency are not specified.
checks.failure: Origin bypass, dependency/zone failure, insufficient surviving capacity, quota exhaustion or missing observability prevents useful service.
checks.verification: Select actual region/topology and versions; test forged/missing edge identity, tenant denial, zone loss and admitted workload with dependency failures. Observe useful completions, rejected demand, pool queue, errors and DB saturation. No deployment or account inspection authorized.
